The mother tree

Literature decides which mechanisms exist. The wording of each plan decides how precisely a commitment can be classified. Comparisons use the deepest level the compared observations share, and the finer detail is kept.

Read the tree

Pillar → subpillar → mechanism family (L2) → mechanism (L3) → objective (L4). Click any node for its definition, literature and placement reasons. Gold nodes hold strategies; grey nodes are empty: the literature names the channel and no plan commits to it.

Pick the countries to compare. For each family the table uses the deepest level every selected country's strategies share: L3 when all of them are classified at a mechanism, otherwise L2, with the share classified finer disclosed per country.
